description: Quill Medical — Renovate configuration
DCB 0129 audit reference: docs/docs/dependencies/automatic-updates.md
DEPENDENCY TIERING STRATEGY
Tier 1 — Clinical
Packages: fhirclient (HAPI FHIR), httpx (EHRbase direct HTTP)
Policy:   No automerge under any circumstances.
Label: tier-1-clinical.
Tier 2 — Infrastructure
Packages: FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, Uvicorn, Pydantic, Alembic, GCP SDKs,
Mantine, React, React Router, Docker base images
Policy:   No automerge; code review required.
Major version bumps labelled major-version-bump.
Tier 3 — Tooling
Packages: eslint, @types/*, pytest, devDependencies,
GitHub Actions, pre-commit hooks
Policy:   No automerge. Every PR is reviewed and added to the merge
queue by hand — see .claude/rules/ci.md.
The tier governs how urgently a human responds and how deeply they
review. It does not change when Renovate opens the PR: every routine
update waits for the Wednesday schedule, whatever its tier.
VULNERABILITY ALERTS
Handled by the top-level vulnerabilityAlerts block, and only there.
Renovate always lets a vulnerability fix skip the schedule and the
rate limits; that cannot be overridden, per tier or otherwise. So a
vulnerability PR for any tier arrives immediately against main,
labelled security, with automerge switched off.
Do NOT put isVulnerabilityAlert in a packageRule. It is a flag
Renovate sets on the rules it generates from GitHub's alerts, not a
matcher: Renovate has no vulnerability matcher at all. A rule carrying
it matches every update of the named packages and marks each one as a
vulnerability fix. That is how the Tier 2 packages came to open a PR
at any hour on hotfix/sec-* branches, labelled security, several
times a day, while the rest of the weekly group waited for Wednesday.
SEVERITY-BASED RESPONSE POLICY
Critical/High in Tier 1 or Tier 2:
Hotfix branch off the latest production tag within 24–48 hrs.
Safety assessment required before merge.
Medium in Tier 2:
Next available working day.
Include in next release if imminent.
Low severity or any Tier 3:
Merge with the next scheduled Wednesday Renovate run.
No hotfix required.
PULL REQUEST LIFECYCLE
draftPR is true so Renovate opens its PRs as drafts, the same way
auto-pr.yml opens every other PR in this repository. Both CI workflows
depend on that: ci.yml's heavy tier and every job in gate-breaking.yml
trigger on ready_for_review, never on opened. A PR opened non-draft that
then never gains a second commit therefore never reports four required
contexts — the two API breaking-change checks and the two DB destructive
migration checks — and can never merge. Marking the PR ready for review
fires them. See .claude/rules/ci.md.
LOCK FILE MAINTENANCE
Renovate only ever bumps the dependencies declared in pyproject.toml
and package.json. Everything those pull in for themselves — Starlette
under FastAPI, aiohttp under pywebpush, Pillow under reportlab, the
npm tooling under jsdom and cspell — stays at whatever version the
lockfile first resolved, however many advisories it accrues. By
September 2026 that layer held every one of the repository's 130
open Dependabot alerts and Renovate had opened a PR for none of them.
lockFileMaintenance re-resolves poetry.lock and yarn.lock from scratch on the
Wednesday schedule, keeping every declared pin and range as it is and
moving only what they already allow. One PR per run, reviewed and
queued by hand like every other.
LABELS
labels replaces the whole list when a rule matches, and the last
matching rule wins. Per-tier and per-update-type labels therefore use
addLabels, which appends, so a major fhirclient bump carries both
tier-1-clinical and major-version-bump.
